lyrics:
[Intro: piano, soft strings, a distant train]

[Verse 1: warm male voice, conversational]
Three a.m., the motorway's all mine
One light on in a signal box, one sign
Somebody's in there with a flask and a chair
I'll never know their name, and they don't care

[Pre-Chorus: drums enter softly]
My kids are sleeping forty miles ahead
Under a roof somebody's watching instead

[Chorus: full band, built to be sung by a crowd]
So whoever's got the night shift
Whoever's on the line
Whoever kept the lights on
And the water running fine
I'll never get to thank you, so I'm singing it instead
Whoever's got the night shift
God bless you. Go to bed.

[Verse 2: voice fuller, guitar chiming]
A nurse who's on her feet since yesterday
A lad who's gritting roads to clear my way
A woman on a switchboard in the dark
Who'll send the right ones if I miss my mark

[Pre-Chorus: drums build]
I used to think I'd made it on my own
I never drove a mile of this alone

[Chorus: full band, crowd joining]
So whoever's got the night shift
Whoever's on the line
Whoever kept the lights on
And the water running fine
I'll never get to thank you, so I'm singing it instead
Whoever's got the night shift
God bless you. Go to bed.

[Guitar Solo: big, lyrical, strings behind]

[Bridge: band drops, piano and voice]
And when it's me who's needed
I hope I'm half as good

[Final Chorus: key up, everyone singing]
Whoever's got the night shift
Whoever's on the line
Whoever kept the lights on
And the water running fine
I'll never get to thank you, so I'm singing it instead
Whoever's got the night shift
God bless you. Go to bed.

[Outro: piano, a key in a front door, a hall light switched off]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 76 BPM, 4/4, E major, up to F# major for the last chorus. A slow, warm, British pop-rock ballad with a singalong chorus.

VOICE: Male, a warm baritone-tenor with an English accent, half-talking the verses with humour and tenderness and opening into a big, plain, tuneful chorus that a crowd can sing. Crowd voices join from the second chorus.

INSTRUMENTS: Piano, a string section, acoustic and chiming electric guitars, bass, a steady drum kit, a lyrical lead guitar solo, a brass pad, crowd voices, a distant train and domestic sounds.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro. 0:14 Verse 1. 0:44 Pre-chorus. 0:56 Chorus 1. 1:30 Verse 2. 2:00 Pre-chorus. 2:12 Chorus 2. 2:46 Guitar solo. 3:06 Bridge. 3:20 Final chorus, key up. 3:56 Outro, a key and a light switch, ends 4:18.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-1990s British pop-rock: warm, big and unfussy, piano and strings leading, a chorus mixed like a football crowd.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'God bless you. Go to bed.' at 1:24.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original thanks angels he cannot see. A man with children knows who the unseen protectors are, and that they have names and shifts.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Alone, noticing, grateful, home.
